heartbeat_contract: run-iteration.ps1 stands down when last_heartbeat is younger than 25 minutes. Protocol: refresh last_heartbeat to NOW at every commit while working, and as the FINAL action of a finished iteration set it ~40 minutes into the past so the next firing takes over immediately instead of standing down against your own heartbeat. Driver-vs-driver overlap is already prevented by the scheduler (MultipleInstances=IgnoreNew), so this guard exists only to keep a live interactive session and the driver off the same branch. Always stamp from PowerShell or Python, never Git Bash date.
next_action: q2's full loop is now proven end-to-end for the first time (see 2026-08-15-spec-flow-findings.md, 'build -> evidence -> verifier accept/reject -> approve -> merge -> reachable-from-main'). Two concrete, contained defects were filed there for q4, both about the operator getting silent success where there should be a signal: (1) PATCH .../tasks/{id} to 'approved' gives no indication when a requirement it serves has rejected or awaiting evidence, even at the document's default 'sketch' rigor where the gate does not block on it - hub/hub/requirement_gate.py's evaluate()/GateRefusal only fires at rigor 'gate'; nothing surfaces the softer case. Every tasks.md splits agent-verifiable from human-only and emits a user test guide.

Use openspec, never the aw-spec skills, and never run AgentWeave against this repo.
Do not call the Agent tool, and do not use workflows or deep research, unless the user requests it. The user HAS requested deep web research, for q7 only.

dead_ends: Git Bash `date` on this machine prints UTC but labels it +0100, so it reads one hour EARLIER than real local time while claiming to be local. PowerShell Get-Date is correct. This matters more than it looks: a last_heartbeat stamped from Git Bash lands an hour in the FUTURE, the driver computes a negative age, concludes a live session holds the branch, and stands down until real time catches up. ALWAYS stamp last_heartbeat from PowerShell (Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:sszzz') or from Python's datetime.now().astimezone().
git add on a path that was deleted and already unstaged aborts the whole add and stages nothing.
npx openspec status --change rejects names starting with a digit; npx openspec archive accepts them. Do not conclude archiving is blocked.
openspec archive prefixes the archive date, producing 2026-08-15-2026-08-13-... in a repo that already dates change names. Rename after archiving.

Keep .ps1 files ASCII-only. PS 5.1 reads BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI and an em dash inside a quoted string breaks parsing several tokens away. Syntax-check with Parser::ParseFile, from the repo root - from hub/ the relative paths resolve to nothing and it reports a spurious FAIL.
PowerShell 5.1 Add-Content -Encoding utf8 writes a BOM. Use UTF8Encoding($false).
Editing a file with Python newline='\n' when git has it as CRLF shows as modified with an empty --numstat. git checkout -- it; it is whitespace-only.
Register-ScheduledTask reports LastTaskResult 267011 before a task has ever run - a stale slot, not an error. 267009 means currently running.

quota_policy: If an iteration dies on a quota/rate limit: DO NOTHING SPECIAL. The Scheduled Task fires every 15 minutes and never unregisters on a failed iteration - it only unregisters past stop_at or with no STATE.json. So the retry loop IS the restart, and it self-heals when the window reopens. Record the quota failure in the work log with its timestamp so the gap is explicable in the morning, and do not burn the remaining budget re-trying inside one iteration.
